title: eval-integration-playbook-v2
content:
Context and intent:
This doc is a practical, implementation-focused playbook for onboarding new models into our evals harness. It is intentionally procedural and pragmatic (notes, commands, gotchas) rather than academic. Use this as a reference when writing data loaders, composing prompt sets, implementing scoring hooks, and wiring CI so we can produce repeatable regression reports for model candidate rollouts.

Goals:
- Fast path: get a new model running against our golden prompt sets and produce a regression report within a day.
- Reliable path: tests and CI that catch common integration issues (tokenization mismatch, shape errors, streaming failures).
- Reproducible reports: delta metrics + bootstrap confidence bands + sample failures for triage.

High-level harness architecture (notes):
- runner/ — CLI entrypoint that starts evaluation jobs. Supports local, k8s-job, and batch GCS-backed runs.
- loaders/ — adapters for dataset sources (local jsonl, GCS manifests, BigQuery extracts, S3). Each adapter returns an iterator of examples and a metadata dict.
- prompts/ — prompt templates + per-task prompt-config (instruction, shot selection, temperature sweep).
- scorers/ — scoring functions that accept (pred, gold, ctx) and emit scalar + optional diagnostic tags.
- reporters/ — diff reporter that composes baseline vs candidate comparisons into a human-readable regression PDF/HTML.
- ci/ — lightweight unit tests, smoke tests, and an integration workflow that runs a small representative sample on PRs.

Recommended repo layout (one canonical layout we use):
- evals-runner/
  - cli.py  # entrypoints: run, dry-run, validate
  - config.yaml  # default runner settings (concurrency, timeouts, logging)
- loaders/
  - base.py  # Loader base class and interfaces (must implement __iter__, metadata())
  - jsonl_loader.py  # streaming, supports gzip, chunked reads, resume tokens
  - gcs_manifest_loader.py  # fetch manifest, stream files in order, parallel prefetch
  - bigquery_loader.py  # export to GCS + pass through jsonl loader (avoid streaming BIGQUERY rows directly)
- prompts/
  - prompt_registry.yaml  # canonical prompt ids, versions, tags, example counts
  - template_tools.py  # canonical format: {{instruction}}
- scorers/
  - exact_match.py
  - normalized_levenshtein.py
  - semantic_similarity.py  # wrapper to call embedding service + cosine sim
- reports/
  - reporter.py  # exports CSV/HTML/JSON+attachments
- ci/
  - smoke_tests.yaml  # GH Actions workflow for PR runs (small sample)
  - unit_tests/

Key implementation patterns and examples (copy/paste friendly):
1) Loader contract (important)
- must be lazy (yield examples) to avoid OOM on large datasets
- should expose metadata: task_id, source_uri, sample_count (if known), schema
- must normalize examples to: {"id": "<string>", "input": "<text>", "gold": "<text>"} or multi-field list for multi-turn
- robust to missing gold (mark as gold: null) — scorers should handle null gold gracefully

Example jsonl_loader behavior notes:
- support compressed files (.gz) transparently
- support a manifest JSONL that lists file shards + optional offsets for resume
- chunk size tuning: default 512 examples per batch for local, 2048 for cluster runs
- prefetch worker pool: default 4, configurable via env RUNNER_PREFETCH=4

2) Prompt sets and versioning
- store prompt templates as small files under prompts/ and a registry that maps prompt_id -> file path + version + tags
- include an explicit "shot_selection" strategy in registry: random, recent_examples, balanced_by_label
- for onboarding, create a "smoke" prompt set with 30 examples and a "full" prompt set matching production size
- always include a small canonical seed for deterministic few-shot selection (seed in prompt config)

3) Scoring functions (robustness tips)
- scorer signature: score(pred_str, gold_str, context=dict) -> {"score": float, "tags": [str], "diagnostic": str}
- avoid brittle token-level comparisons — use normalized whitespace, punctuation stripping, casefolding when appropriate
- for generative tasks: provide both exact/strict and fuzzy/semantic scorers; include both in regression table
- for rankings: use NDCG@k and compute pairwise swap counts; expose ties handling strategy
- include an "error" code field when scorer cannot compute (e.g., non-text output) so the reporter can surface sample traces

4) Regression report generation
- Always produce: per-task aggregate metrics (mean, std, sample-count), delta (candidate - baseline), p-value via bootstrap (1000 resamples default), and effect-size (Cohen's d)
- For top regressions, produce a sample-of-failure table: show prompt, gold, baseline output, candidate output, scorer tags, token-diff (side-by-side)
- Attach trace logs (request id, latency, model version tag) to sample rows for debugging network/serving issues
- Use color-coding for deltas (red: degrade > threshold, green: improve > threshold). Thresholds live in config.report_thresholds

5) CI wiring (conservative and fast)
- PR-level: run unit tests + small smoke eval (30 examples across 3 tasks). Smoke should be deterministic and fast (<5 minutes). Smoke is gated and must pass before merge.
- Nightly: run full regression for important models (baseline candidates) and upload artifact to S3/GCS, create Confluence draft page with automated summary and attach PDF report.
- For model-serving changes, run the same loader/scorer suite against the candidate in a dedicated staging endpoint; if latency or error-rate increases beyond thresholds, fail the job.
- GH Actions patterns: use matrix with python versions but keep matrix small; cache wheels and deps with actions/cache keyed by poetry.lock + pip cache
- Reuse test fixtures: small jsonl under ci/fixtures/ for reproducible smoke runs

6) Stability and flaky test mitigation
- Mark non-deterministic tests with xfail and track flakiness in a flaky-tests dashboard (CSV in infra/ci/flaky.csv)
- Where randomness is unavoidable (sampling shots), fix seeds in CI and log the seed in the report for reproducibility
- Implement retry-on-transient-failures for network calls with exponential backoff (max 3 attempts); log each retry with reason

7) Operational notes for model onboarding flow (practical steps)
- Step 0: owner creates an eval ticket JIRA-EVAL-<n> and links model artifact (container tag or model registry id).
- Step 1: add prompt id and dataset manifest to prompt_registry.yaml and create a 30-example smoke set in ci/fixtures/ with review from task SME.
- Step 2: implement loader if data source is custom; follow loader contract and add unit tests for edge cases (missing gold, compressed shards).
- Step 3: write scorer(s) or pick existing scorer ids; add scorer unit tests covering degenerate outputs (empty string, non-utf8).
- Step 4: run local runner: python -m evals_run ner --config config.yaml --manifest path/to/manifest.jsonl --output outdir/
- Step 5: open PR with smoke results and link JIRA ticket, request review from SME and infra owner.

8) Common gotchas (lessons learned)
- Tokenizer mismatch: different tokenizers between baseline and candidate can change generation prefixes — verify tokenizer + eos handling; include tokenization step in warmup smoke.
- Streaming vs non-streaming responses: our harness expects final text; streaming partials must be concatenated and validated.
- Latency spikes in CI: if a single example takes >30s, mark it and skip in smoke runs; create a separate perf-triage job.
- Data leakage: avoid pulling training data as prompts (put a quarantine check in loader that flags any example matching training-set hashes).

9) Mini-checklist for PR reviewers (copy into PR template):
- [ ] Loader follows lazy iterator contract and has unit tests
- [ ] Prompts registered and smoke set added
- [ ] Scorers implemented and have edge-case tests
- [ ] PR includes smoke eval artifact (results CSV) and short summary
- [ ] CI workflows updated if needed (new secrets or larger matrix)

10) TODOs and open questions (notes to self)
- Evaluate adding a standardized "manifest.json" schema for dataset provenance (hashes, source, extraction query).
- Decide canonical place for semantic similarity scorer models (embed-service vs local CACHED model).
- Improve reporter visuals — consider embedding small diffs inline rather than linking to attachments.
- Explore auto-triage heuristics for sample failures using clustering of failure embeddings to suggest root causes.

References and links:
- GH-PR-7890: initial evals runner refactor (see comments on loader contract)
- CONFLUENCE-1234: Eval onboarding playbook (high-level)
- JIRA-EVAL-456: onboarding ticket template

Contact: @maya.chen in #applied-ml-evals, ping arjun or lucia for loader/scorer reviews.

Quick command cheat-sheet:
- Local dry run (30-sample smoke): python -m evals_run run --manifest ci/fixtures/smoke_ner.jsonl --prompt prompt_registry.yaml --out ./out/smoke
- Full run (cluster): evals-runner submit --manifest gs://my-bucket/manifests/task_v1.jsonl --config config.yaml --runner k8s --concurrency 32
- Generate report from results: python reports/reporter.py --baseline out/baseline/results.jsonl --candidate out/candidate/results.jsonl --out out/reports/regression.html

End of playbook. Keep this file iterative — prefer small, targeted sections over monolithic docs.
